items.title: CISA Adds One Known Exploited Vulnerability to Catalog
items.one_liner: SonicWall SonicOS SSLVPN single-factor authentication flaw added to CISA KEV catalog due to active exploitation.
items.summary: CISA has added a single new vulnerability, CVE-2026-19868 affecting SonicWall SonicOS SSLVPN single-factor authentication, to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog. The inclusion follows evidence of active exploitation in the wild, posing high risks to enterprise networks. Under Binding Operational Directive 26-04, Federal Civilian Executive Branch agencies must rapidly remediate catalog vulnerabilities that grant total post-exploitation control. Private organizations are also strongly encouraged to adopt this risk-based prioritization.
items.bottom_line: Federal agencies must rapidly patch SonicWall CVE-2026-19868 following confirmation of active exploitation.

items.title: CVE-2026-102895: GPUStack GPUStack Improper Authentication Vulnerability
items.one_liner: A critical authentication bypass in GPUStack allows unauthenticated administrative access and RCE, demanding immediate patching under CISA guidance.
items.summary: GPUStack contains an improper authentication vulnerability that permits unauthenticated administrative access, user and model changes, persistent administrator API-key creation, disclosure of worker and cloud-provider secrets, and arbitrary code execution. CISA added the flaw to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog under BOD 26-04, requiring federal agencies to apply mitigations by November 12, 2026. Organizations must evaluate internet exposure and ensure adherence to these patching guidelines. If mitigations are unavailable, administrators must discontinue use of the product.
items.bottom_line: Unauthenticated attackers can gain full administrative control and execute arbitrary code on vulnerable GPUStack instances.

items.title: France accuses Iran of supermarket fridge hacking
items.one_liner: France blames Iran's IRGC for unprecedented cyber-attacks that sabotaged supermarket refrigeration units and spoiled food across Europe.
items.summary: France has accused Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps of orchestrating cyber-attacks that maliciously raised the temperatures of supermarket refrigeration units across the country last month, spoiling tons of food. French Foreign Minister Jean-Noël Barrot condemned the operation as an unprecedented act of sabotage and announced upcoming sanctions alongside the summoning of the Iranian ambassador. Parisian prosecutors opened investigations into members of the IRGC's Shahid Kaveh cyber unit. Similar secondary hacking waves subsequently struck supermarkets across Belgium, Luxembourg, Sweden, Ireland, the Netherlands, Estonia, and Finland.
key_facts: Targeted software: Danfoss refrigeration management software
items.bottom_line: State-sponsored cyber-attacks targeting Danfoss refrigeration software have compromised commercial food storage across multiple European nations.

items.title: Nvidia shares tumble over investigation into Huang's affair with alleged Chinese spy
items.one_liner: Nvidia loses $250 billion in market value following an investigation into CEO Jensen Huang's relationship with an alleged Chinese spy.
items.summary: Nvidia shares dropped roughly 4% after the chipmaker announced an independent investigation into CEO Jensen Huang's extramarital affair with an alleged Chinese spy, Alice Huang. US intelligence officials warned that the Nvidia boss was targeted in a Beijing espionage campaign, though China rejected the allegations as groundless. The fallout wiped approximately $250 billion off Nvidia's market value, while competitors saw gains as broader US markets recovered. Congressional committees have also requested Jensen Huang to appear for a closed-door briefing regarding corporate security protocols.
items.bottom_line: Nvidia faces intense congressional scrutiny and market volatility after confirming an investigation into CEO Jensen Huang's links to an alleged Chinese intelligence operative.

items.title: Attackers Exploit Third-Party Provider to Raid French Bank Crédit Mutuel Arkéa
items.one_liner: A major European banking breach via a third-party service provider underscores supply-chain vulnerabilities in financial institutions.
items.summary: Hackers infiltrated French cooperative bank Crédit Mutuel Arkéa by exploiting a third-party service provider's platform, utilizing the bank's own account to execute fraudulent transactions totaling up to $133 million. The stolen funds were funneled through other banking institutions, converted into USDC and USDT stablecoins, and aggressively swapped for privacy-focused cryptocurrencies like Monero. Although customer assets remained unaffected and operations have gradually resumed, the lack of immediate public disclosure allowed attackers to rapidly launder substantial sums before authorities could freeze them. The Paris prosecutor's cybercrime unit and France's cybercrime police are currently leading an active investigation into the breach, while the bank strengthens its security posture and warns users of heightened phishing risks.
key_facts: Stolen amount: Up to $133 million (approx. €100-118 million)
Investigating agency: Paris prosecutor's cybercrime unit
items.bottom_line: Financial institutions remain acutely vulnerable to multi-million dollar thefts via compromised third-party vendor platforms rather than direct network breaches.

items.title: Fake GitHub Security Tools Infect Over 2,000 PCs With Malware
items.one_liner: Threat actors are weaponizing fake GitHub security tooling and Visual Studio projects with advanced evasion and multi-payload stealers, posing a direct threat to infosec workstations.
items.summary: Cybersecurity firm Doctor Web discovered a two-year-old malware campaign hiding malicious code inside fake GitHub security tools and Visual Studio projects targeting blockchain enthusiasts and information security professionals, infecting over 2,000 PCs. The projects use PowerShell scripts and downloader files disguised as Windows Photos components to deploy a modular app called Microsoft.exe that disables Windows Defender, UAC, system restore, and removes competing antivirus products. The malware employs advanced evasion techniques such as direct system calls and process hollowing before deploying payloads including AsyncRAT, a crypto-wallet clipper, and a broad credential stealer that harvests browser and VPN data.
items.bottom_line: Malware hidden in fake GitHub security tools has infected over 2,000 PCs and disables security controls.

claims.support_span: Cybersecurity firm Doctor Web has found malware hidden in GitHub projects that look like security tools.

claims.support_span: The campaign targets blockchain game fans and, more recently, information security professionals. The researchers discovered that more than 2,000 PCs were infected.

items.title: CVE-2026-120408 (HIGH 8.0): The All-in-One Video Gallery WordPress plugin before 5.1.0 does not escape a video's stored thumbnail URL bef…
items.one_liner: A Stored XSS vulnerability in the All-in-One Video Gallery WordPress plugin lets Subscribers compromise administrators.
items.summary: The All-in-One Video Gallery WordPress plugin prior to version 5.1.0 fails to escape stored video thumbnail URLs when outputting them in the admin video list and neglects sanitization outside its editor. This allows authenticated users with Subscriber roles to execute Stored Cross-Site Scripting attacks against administrators. The vulnerability carries a CVSS base score of 8.0 and was published on November 6, 2026.
items.bottom_line: Subscriber-level users can execute Stored XSS attacks against administrators via unescaped video thumbnail URLs in plugin versions prior to 5.1.0.

items.title: ARTEX attack https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/security/blog/2026/11/05/threat-actors-use-agentic-ai-tooling-to-find-and-abuse-exposed-secrets/ @secharvester
items.one_liner: Threat actors are using agentic AI frameworks like ARTEX to rapidly mine public GitHub repositories for exposed cloud credentials.
items.summary: Microsoft Threat Intelligence observed threat actors using the agentic AI offensive framework ARTEX to scan public GitHub repositories for exposed API keys, credentials, and cloud secrets at an accelerated pace. Attackers successfully leveraged compromised multi-tenant application credentials and service principals—such as from IP 199.19.77.84—to conduct cloud resource discovery and exfiltrate data from Azure Key Vaults and Storage Accounts in as little as five minutes. Microsoft advises organizations to scan codebases, remove secrets, and immediately rotate exposed credentials.

items.title: Barracuda Networks is your new best friend (Barracuda Email Security Gateway Pre-Auth Remote Root RCE CVE-2026-116606 / CVE-2026-111560)
items.one_liner: Chaining Barracuda ESG CVE-2026-116606 and CVE-2026-111560 enables unauthenticated remote root command execution on edge appliances.
items.summary: WatchTowr Labs analyzed two critical vulnerabilities affecting Barracuda's Email Security Gateway and related edge appliances: CVE-2026-116606, an authentication bypass with a CVSS score of 9.3, and CVE-2026-111560, an OS command injection flaw scored 8.6. When chained together, these flaws allow unauthenticated remote attackers to achieve command execution at the root level. Barracuda released specific patches—designated Patch-1 and Patch-2—to resolve these issues in version 9.4.0.029. The analysis underscores the ongoing risk posed by edge devices that inspect incoming mail with high privileges.

items.title: Claude Code is accidentally exposing secrets all over GitHub
items.one_liner: Claude Code's automatic shell command approval behavior is leaking plain-text API tokens and database credentials into public GitHub repositories.
items.summary: Claude Code settings files embedded in public GitHub repositories are leaking sensitive information, including database passwords, API tokens, and root logins. The leakage occurs because user approvals for automated shell commands, when saved with the 'Yes, and don't ask again' option, write raw commands containing embedded secrets directly into local settings.json files. While the file is normally excluded via global .gitignore lists, developer oversights have resulted in thousands of instances being shared publicly. Anthropic documentation typically relies on local gitignore protection to prevent exposure.
items.bottom_line: Developers using Claude Code's persistent command approvals risk exposing live database credentials and API keys if local settings files are committed.

items.title: Cisco Informational for Emergency Distrust of eMudhra Root and Intermediate Certificate Authorities
items.one_liner: Cisco issued an informational advisory regarding the emergency distrust of eMudhra intermediate CAs due to weak key generation.
items.summary: Between October 17 and October 20, 2026, a critical security compromise was uncovered involving Certificate Authorities managed by eMudhra. A security researcher demonstrated that private keys for eight eMudhra intermediate certificates were fundamentally broken due to an error in their Key Generation Ceremony in April 2025, enabling anyone to brute-force acquire the private keys within seconds. Cisco issued an informational security advisory regarding the emergency distrust of these eMudhra root and intermediate certificate authorities across products. Similar advisories have been published by Cisco Talos and Splunk.
key_facts: Compromised entities: Eight eMudhra intermediate certificates
items.bottom_line: Compromised eMudhra intermediate certificate keys demand immediate emergency distrust and replacement across enterprise PKI trust stores.

items.summary: Attackers hijacked compromised Identity and Access Management (IAM) credentials associated with cloud data platform Qubole's AWS account to breach customer cloud environments and harvest sensitive data. items.title: Dokploy: the validator allows the backtick — a member's database password change is host RCE, 9.9 on the vendor's own vector (v0.31.0, live-proven)
items.one_liner: Dokploy v0.31.0 suffers from a critical RCE vulnerability where flawed password and username validation permits command injection via backticks and semicolons.
items.summary: A critical vulnerability in Dokploy v0.31.0 allows authenticated organization members with service creation permissions to achieve remote code execution as root on the host container. The issue stems from an incomplete database password regex validator in packages/server/src/db/schema/utils.ts, which bans various shell meta-characters but mistakenly permits backticks. When changing database passwords for Postgres or MySQL, the new password is wrapped in single quotes inside a double-quoted shell command, allowing bash command substitution via backticks. Additionally, the databaseUser parameter lacks any validation entirely, permitting semicolon-based command injection. This grants an attacker who can deploy databases full access to the host's Docker socket and database credentials.

items.one_liner: Ghostscript before 10.08.0 suffers from a -dSAFER bypass via .putgstringcopy enabling arbitrary code execution.
items.summary: Ghostscript versions prior to 10.08.0 contain a -dSAFER bypass vulnerability in the .putgstringcopy procedure within gs_fonts.ps. items.title: Re: [musl] Re: [oss-security] "sshole": password authentication bypass: OpenSSH + musl libc
items.one_liner: Musl libc maintainer rejects behavioral build-time options in response to OpenSSH authentication discussions, planning standard null returns in future releases.
items.summary: In an ongoing oss-security mailing list discussion regarding an OpenSSH password authentication bypass linked to musl libc, maintainer Rich Felker addressed proposed build options. items.title: USN-9011-1: pyasn1 vulnerabilities
items.one_liner: Multiple denial-of-service vulnerabilities in pyasn1 allow remote attackers to exhaust CPU and memory via crafted ASN.1 data.
items.summary: Security vulnerabilities have been discovered in pyasn1 concerning its handling of BER, CER, and DER encoded data across multiple Ubuntu LTS releases. The issues involve unbounded size limits for long-form tag identifiers, quadratic time complexity when processing OBJECT IDENTIFIER and RELATIVE-OID arcs, and improper conversion of decoded REAL values to Python floats. An attacker can exploit these flaws by supplying crafted untrusted ASN.1 data to cause excessive CPU and memory consumption, resulting in a denial of service.

items.title: patrick1357/impnxc-cloak — Wire and behavioural de-fingerprinting patches for impacket and NetExec
items.one_liner: A new tool allows red teamers to patch Impacket and NetExec to evade EDR and network monitoring by mimicking legitimate Windows traffic.
items.summary: The impnxc-cloak project provides a set of patches for Impacket and NetExec designed to strip network and behavioural fingerprints that security tools use to detect these frameworks. items.one_liner: An exported activity in Microsoft Authenticator allowed unprivileged Android apps to steal enterprise tokens via a flawed signature check.
items.summary: Researchers discovered a high-severity vulnerability tracked as CVE-2026-80097 in Microsoft Authenticator for Android, caused by an improperly secured and exported activity. An unprivileged Android app with zero permissions could invoke AccountChooserActivity, spoof the caller UID, and leverage a flawed signature check to obtain valid delegation tokens for any installed first-party Microsoft application like Teams. This granted attackers full delegated access to the victim's work mailboxes, files, and calendar without requiring any user interaction beyond having an active work account signed into the broker. Microsoft has issued a security patch to resolve the issue.

items.one_liner: Ettercap up to 0.8.4.1 contains an NTLM-parsing out-of-bounds read vulnerability.

items.one_liner: Ettercap up to v0.8.4.1 suffers from a telnet dissector stack buffer underwrite exploitable for root privilege corruption.
items.summary: CVE-2026-125406 identifies a stack buffer underwrite vulnerability in Ettercap versions up to 0.8.4.1. The flaw resides in the telnet dissector within src/dissectors/ec_telnet.c, where backspace handling decrements the output pointer without a lower bound check. Attackers can send a crafted telnet stream featuring more backspaces than preceding characters to write below the stack buffer. This corrupts the stack of the Ettercap process, which typically executes with root privileges.
items.bottom_line: Unchecked backspace handling in Ettercap's telnet dissector allows low-bound memory corruption under root privileges.

items.title: CVE-2026-115864: Monoceros versions before 0.30 for Perl allow a request declaring a large Content-Length to kill a worker by exhausting memory
items.one_liner: Monoceros before 0.30 for Perl allows remote attackers to trigger worker out-of-memory crashes via requests with oversized Content-Length headers.
items.summary: Monoceros versions prior to 0.30 for Perl contain a memory exhaustion vulnerability tracked as CVE-2026-115864 (CWE-789). The issue arises because the application reads incoming request bodies in a loop using sysread for the entire declared Content-Length at once. Perl automatically grows its read buffer to match the specified size before any data arrives, allowing a remote attacker to send a request with an excessively large Content-Length value and force worker processes to exit with uncatchable out-of-memory errors. Repeated requests of only a few bytes can thus trigger continuous worker restarts and denial of service. Users are advised to upgrade to Monoceros version 0.30 or later.
key_facts: Affected software: Monoceros for Perl versions before 0.30
Weakness: CWE-789 (Memory Allocation with Excessive Size Value)
items.bottom_line: Perl web applications using Monoceros prior to version 0.30 must upgrade to mitigate a remote denial-of-service vector via memory exhaustion.

items.title: CVE-2026-119078: Apache Commons Codec: Blake3 doFinalize is stateless; the documented KDF example derives identical keys
items.one_liner: Apache Commons Codec Blake3 doFinalize is stateless, leading to identical key derivation in documented examples for versions 1.16.0 to 1.22.0.
items.summary: A security advisory for Apache Commons Codec versions 1.16.0 through 1.22.0 highlights CVE-2026-119078, centered on stateless behavior in the Blake3 doFinalize method. While the class Javadoc incorrectly documented that consecutive doFinalize calls would yield different output by depending on previously finalized bytes, doFinalize actually does not alter the underlying hash state. Consequently, key-derivation examples demonstrating two consecutive doFinalize calls produce identical keys instead of separate ones. Version 1.23.0 corrects the misleading documentation, but developers must update their code to request combined lengths in a single call when deriving multiple keys.
items.bottom_line: Developers relying on Apache Commons Codec Blake3 key derivation must check applications for repeated doFinalize calls, as upgrading to 1.23.0 corrects documentation but leaves stateless behavior unchanged.

items.title: Minerva: Reinforcement Learning with Verifiable Rewards for Cyber Threat Intelligence LLMs
items.one_liner: Minerva applies reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards to significantly improve CTI large language models.
items.summary: Minerva is a unified dataset and training pipeline designed to improve large language models for Cyber Threat Intelligence (CTI) tasks using reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards (RLVR). Because CTI standards define canonical identifiers and schemas, Minerva pairs subtasks with task-specific verifiers to score structured outputs and identifier predictions deterministically. To overcome reward sparsity during rollout, the authors introduce MinervaRL, an auxiliary self-training mechanism that generates verified trajectories and distills them back into the model. Evaluated across multiple backbones and CTI benchmarks, MinervaRL significantly outperforms base models and standard GRPO approaches.
key_facts: Improvement: 15.8 percentage points over base models
items.bottom_line: Using verifiable rewards in reinforcement learning enables LLMs to produce structured, highly accurate cyber threat intelligence outputs.

items.title: AI Agents Are Testing the Limits of Zero-Trust Security
items.one_liner: AI agent architectures and vibe coding practices are testing the limits of zero-trust security by exposing systems to rapid context recovery and de-authentication attacks.
items.summary: Researchers and teams utilizing multi-agent AI frameworks face fundamental security hurdles in maintaining zero-trust guarantees within orchestrating architectures. While agents are programmed with checkpoints to delete historic relevance to prevent decision skewing, context recovery attacks can trick models into exposing purged information. Furthermore, relying on automated off-the-shelf models for software development—known as vibe coding—exposes entire codebases to untrusted external entities and sweeping vulnerabilities. Experiments conducted at Queen’s University Belfast demonstrate that agentic orchestration can accelerate automated de-authentication attacks down to windows of two to three seconds.
items.bottom_line: AI agentic workflows and vibe coding introduce severe cyber risks, enabling rapid de-authentication attacks and context recovery exploits that bypass zero-trust safeguards.

items.summary: The Hugging Face Open ASR Leaderboard has expanded its private evaluation data to include Egyptian and Nigerian accented English, in collaboration with Liva AI. This initiative aims to improve the representation of diverse accents in speech-recognition benchmarks and enhance trust by using held-out data from real-world consumer products. The leaderboard now categorizes accents based on Kachru’s Three Circles model to provide a more granular breakdown of model performance. This effort is part of a broader push to minimize 'benchmaxxing' and ensure ASR models perform reliably across global English dialects.
items.bottom_line: ASR model evaluation is shifting toward more representative, real-world datasets to ensure performance across global English accents.

items.title: Modernising threat hunting: Using Semantic Search to Find Risky AI Agent Behavior
items.one_liner: Semantic vector search over AI agent session logs helps security teams catch risky automated behaviors.
items.summary: Security analysts are exploring vector search and semantic querying over stored AI agent session logs—such as those from Claude Code and Cursor—to detect risky agent behavior that traditional keyword and regex rules miss. Because AI agents dynamically choose actions based on high-level user prompts, individual steps may appear benign while the session as a whole creates security risks, such as accidentally committing sensitive files to public repositories. By embedding interaction turns at ingest and performing semantic similarity searches, teams can flag anomalous workflows for human review without relying on costly per-session LLM evaluations.
items.bottom_line: Vector search over stored AI coding agent sessions enables scalable detection of risky, multi-step agent actions.

claims.text: Semantic search using vector embeddings stored in Elastic allows hunting for risky AI agent sessions.
claims.support_span: In this article, we review using vector search to hunt risky AI sessions. I stored six months of my own Claude Code and Cursor sessions as semantic vectors in Elastic and searched them instead of handing every session to an LLM.

claims.text: AI agent tasks can involve benign individual actions that combine to create security flaws, such as committing project files to an external repository.
claims.support_span: As an example of something hard to detect in agent chats, a developer asks their coding agent to tidy up a data export. The agent reads a CSV, which turns out to contain customer records. It runs git init , adds a remote repository, commits, and pushes to the repository.

items.title: Introducing pathrunner: An AWS privilege escalation framework
items.one_liner: Datadog released pathrunner, an open-source offensive security framework for automating AWS IAM privilege escalation paths.
items.summary: Datadog Security Labs has released pathrunner, a modular cloud-native offensive security framework designed to automate the exploitation of AWS IAM privilege escalation paths cataloged in pathfinding.cloud and instantiated in Pathfinding Labs. The framework helps defenders and red teams prioritize misconfigurations by demonstrating their actual exploitability and impact. Unlike traditional Active Directory environments where attacks pivot via TCP sessions between workloads, cloud environments typically involve credential-based escalation from one AWS identity to another. pathrunner automates credential import, exploit module execution, and identity switching to validate attack paths.
items.bottom_line: pathrunner automates AWS IAM privilege escalation exploitation, enabling security teams to validate and prioritize cloud misconfigurations.

items.title: Which LLM writes the best code? A 2026 comparison
items.one_liner: A structured pilot framework across seven criteria helps development teams select and manage coding LLMs effectively.
items.summary: Selecting the best LLM for coding requires a structured framework rather than relying on stale public leaderboards, given frequent model releases from Anthropic, Google, OpenAI, and SpaceXAI. Teams should evaluate models across seven core criteria—code correctness, security, maintainability, repository context, latency, cost, and governance—by piloting them directly on internal repositories. According to Stack Overflow's 2026 Developer Survey, roughly 80% of developers use multiple AI coding tools and frequently switch between them. Independent verification via CI quality gates remains essential to catch insecure patterns or maintainability issues regardless of the model chosen.
key_facts: Adoption: ~80% of developers use 2+ AI tools
items.bottom_line: Evaluate coding LLMs using repository-specific pilots and CI checks instead of public leaderboards.

items.title: How I Found a $113,337 AF_ALG Linux Local Privilege Escalation Before Copy Fail
items.one_liner: A retrospective look at uncovering a $113,337 Linux kernel privilege escalation flaw in the AF_ALG cryptographic subsystem via unprivileged socket APIs.
items.summary: Security researcher Muhammad Alifa Ramdhan details the discovery of CVE-2025-39964, a critical race condition vulnerability in the Linux kernel's AF_ALG cryptographic subsystem that earned a $113,337 reward via Google's kernelCTF. Exploiting out-of-bounds access stemming from how AF_ALG handles inputs across unprivileged sockets, an ordinary user can escalate privileges to root or achieve container escape. Present in the kernel since 2011, this vulnerability preceded the widely known 'Copy Fail' flaw but highlights the same underlying kernel attack surface.
items.bottom_line: Unprivileged access to the Linux kernel's AF_ALG subsystem harbors deep race condition vulnerabilities capable of full privilege escalation and container escape.

items.title: Hide your slop PR descriptions behind <details><summary>
items.one_liner: Using HTML details tags in GitHub PR descriptions hides bulky AI-generated text behind human-curated summaries to improve code review efficiency.
items.summary: AI coding agents like Claude Code and Codex generate comprehensive and accurate pull request descriptions that can overwhelm readers with excessive technical detail. items.bottom_line: Hide bulky AI-generated PR descriptions inside HTML details and summary tags to keep code reviews readable.

items.title: NHS breach helpline left staff carrying a 'significant emotional burden'
items.one_liner: An un-redacted NHS FOI spreadsheet led to a distressing helpline assignment for staff who faced severe emotional strain without adequate preparation.
items.summary: The Royal Cornwall Hospitals NHS Trust established an 11-week helpline following a data breach that exposed sickness absence and health records of 8,003 individuals due to an un-redacted pivot table in an FOI response. Staff assigned to the helpline faced distressed callers and potential domestic abuse situations with minimal preparation, short training, and no prior support, leading to a significant emotional burden. Many handlers learned of their own data exposure while working the helpline and had to maintain ordinary duties alongside extended contact center shifts. Although the review findings have been circulated and published online, the incident underscores severe welfare oversight during crisis responses.
items.bottom_line: Failing to scrub underlying pivot tables from FOI disclosures led to a major data exposure that severely impacted both victims and unprepared internal support staff.

items.title: Silverseal: Silverseal is an open-source Linux bootkit and rootkit framework and the first public ARM64 bootkit for Linux distros…
items.one_liner: This open-source Rust framework provides a complete demonstration of pre-OS persistence and kernel-module loading on ARM64 and x64 Linux architectures.
items.summary: Silverseal is an open-source research framework written in Rust that demonstrates the first public ARM64 and x64 Linux UEFI bootkit and rootkit workflow. The bootkit replaces GRUB EFI binaries, intercepts the Linux boot-image path, detours the kernel zstd decompressor, and redirects a late-initcall entry to insert a stager and worker into kernel code caves. After a ten-second delay, the worker executes /sbin/insmod to load a Kbuild-managed Rust kernel module from the root filesystem. The repository provides architecture-specific setup and recovery scripts for environments like Ubuntu and WSL2, utilizing specific kernel configurations such as CONFIG_RUST=y.
items.bottom_line: Researchers can now study a public, working ARM64 and x64 UEFI bootkit and Rust rootkit implementation for Linux.

items.title: CVE-2026-124077: Apache Commons Codec: NUL bytes in tree entry names cause Git/SWHID identifier collisions (GitIdentifiers class)
items.one_liner: Apache Commons Codec versions 1.22.0 to 1.23.0 allowed NUL bytes in GitIdentifiers tree entries, causing SWHID and Git identifier collisions.
items.summary: A security vulnerability designated CVE-2026-124077 affects Apache Commons Codec versions 1.22.0 prior to 1.23.0 within the GitIdentifiers class. The class failed to reject NUL bytes in tree entry names, allowing crafted names to cause two different directory trees to serialize to identical bytes and generate colliding Git tree identifiers or Software Heritage Identifiers (SWHIDs). Because standard filesystems disallow NUL bytes, typical filesystem-walking applications are unaffected, leaving exposure limited to applications processing archive formats like ZIP or direct API inputs. Users are advised to upgrade to version 1.23.0 to resolve the issue.
items.bottom_line: Java applications using Apache Commons Codec to build Git trees or SWHIDs from untrusted archive names must upgrade to version 1.23.0 to prevent identifier collisions.

The Atlantic migration route has proved particularly deadly, with Spanish rights group Walking Borders recording 635 deaths between January and May 2026. items.bottom_line: A migrant shipwreck off the coast of Senegal has killed at least 39 people, compounding the exceptionally high death toll on the Atlantic migration route to Europe.

items.title: Installing the Fix for an Exploited WordPress Flaw Can Expose Some Sites One Last Time
items.summary: Some WordPress sites can still be attacked while they install the fix for an actively exploited flaw, according to Umut Bayram, the Picus Security researcher who found it. The update that installs the fix still unpacks its files using the site's old, unpatched code, so an attacker who strikes at the right moment can run code on the server. The researcher advises blocking web access to the site's wp-content/upgrade folder before updating. The flaw, tracked as CVE-2026-119977, affects WordPress 4.7 through 7.1.3. During a core update that uses a complete package, WordPress unpacks a copy of the new version into a temporary folder inside wp-content/upgrade.

items.title: Locating the source of a mysterious beep with Claude
items.one_liner: A developer used Claude Code to build an acoustic triangulation web app inspired by academic research to locate a mysterious beeping device.
items.summary: Faced with a mysterious, intermittently beeping device buried in a box room, software developer Simon Willison used Claude Code to build 'Beep Locator,' a software system that triangulates the source of acoustic signals using multiple commodity devices. Running on a Python web server with client interfaces connected via WebSockets, the app utilizes device-to-device audio ranging inspired by the 2007 research paper 'BeepBeep' by Chunyi Peng et al. By combining rough manual coordinate dragging with automated Fast Fourier Transform beep detection and interval measurement, the system successfully isolated the sound to within 40 centimeters, leading to an ancient carbon monoxide detector.
items.bottom_line: Claude Code can effectively build complex custom acoustic triangulation tools using commodity hardware to solve precise real-world localization problems.

items.summary: GitHub is introducing a native egress firewall for GitHub-hosted Actions runners to bring network controls to builds. While network allowlists are vital for software supply chain security, StepSecurity's Harden-Runner offers broader capabilities that distinguish it from a basic native firewall. Specifically, Harden-Runner supports multiple runner environments including Linux, Windows, and macOS across GitHub-hosted, self-hosted, Kubernetes, and bare-metal servers. It builds automated network baselines from previous runs to detect anomalies, correlates process and file events to specific workflow steps, and provides cross-repository visibility proven against real-world supply chain attacks.
items.bottom_line: Teams relying solely on GitHub's native egress firewall miss critical cross-platform coverage, behavioral baselining, and step-level anomaly detection offered by specialized runtime agents.

items.title: Your Experts Have Partners. There's HOPE for Keeping Them Together
items.summary: Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) models have enabled state-of-the-art LLMs to be scaled to hundreds of billions of parameters, but they come with a fundamental and costly caveat: every expert MLP must occupy memory at inference time, even though the vast majority are idle for any given token. For example, Qwen3.5-122B has 256 experts in each of its 48 MoE layers, and 95% of its ~250 GB parameter memory footprint is taken up entirely by these expert MLPs alone. However, for any given token, only 8 experts in each layer are actually used. Expert pruning is one of the most direct fixes to this memory bottleneck. That is, permanently delete the least useful experts.

items.summary: A Massachusetts judge has denied a motion to dismiss the murder case against Lindsay Clancy, who is accused of killing her three children in 2023. The ruling clears the path for prosecutors to pursue a second trial, with a scheduling discussion set for November 16.

items.title: Kochi Corporation plans water security assessment to strengthen city’s resilience
items.one_liner: IIT Palakkad is helping Kochi Corporation launch a water security assessment to tackle flooding, pollution, and scarcity.
items.summary: The Kochi Corporation is planning a comprehensive water security assessment project to improve the city's resilience against water scarcity, pollution, flooding, and sewage challenges. items.title: Keralam Excise dept. bans issuance of new liquor licences until promulgation of Keralam  govt.’s liquor policy
items.one_liner: A political row over hasty bar licensing forces a blanket freeze on new alcohol permits in Kerala until late November.
items.summary: The Keralam Excise department has banned the issuance of new liquor licences, including bars and wine and beer parlours, until the government promulgates its official alcohol policy for the 2026-27 fiscal year on November 30. The directive follows a political controversy where the government shifted Excise Commissioner Seeram Samabasiva Rao after officials hastily reclassified bars and approved lounge bars at Cochin International Airport Limited without ministerial sign-off. As a result, 28 pending applications from four-star hotels have been put on hold while the ruling alliance reviews delegation and political sensitivities.
items.bottom_line: Keralam's Excise department banned issuing new liquor licences until the alcohol policy is released on November 30.
